rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā is a rebuke and deterrent: God will neither grant the dying person's request to return nor accept it.
rows.anchor: كلا حرف ردع وزجر، أي: لا نجيبه إلى ما طلب ولا نقبل منه

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Every dying wrongdoer inevitably utters this request.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: أي لا بد أن يقولها لا محالة كل محتضر ظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the request is merely speech without action; even if returned, the person would not act righteously and would be lying, as 6:28 says.
rows.anchor: لأنها كلمة، أي: سؤاله الرجوع ليعمل صالحا هو كلام منه، وقول لا عمل معه

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: He portrays the dying person asking to return, then God answers that this is only a word he says.
rows.anchor: محمد بن كعب القرظي: {حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد الله مولى غفرة
rows.claim: When God says kallā, it means that the speaker has lied.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد الله مولى غفرة: إذا سمعت الله يقول: {كلا} فإنما يقول: كذب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda transmits al-Alāʾ ibn Ziyād's advice to imagine death has arrived and one's request for reprieve was granted, then obey God.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله تعالى: {حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The unbeliever longs to return for obedience to God, not to rejoin family or tribe; the living should act on that wish.
rows.anchor: والله ما تمنى أن يرجع إلى أهل ولا إلى عشيرة، ولكن تمنى أن يرجع فيعمل بطاعة الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A dead unbeliever sees his place in the Fire, asks to return and repent, but is told his allotted life is over; the grave then constricts and its creatures torment him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حازم، عن أبي هريرة قال: إذا وضع -يعني: الكافر-في قبره، فيرى مقعده من النار

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha describes black or dark snakes biting sinful people in their graves until they meet at the body's middle, identifying this as barzakh punishment.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن عائشة، أنها قالت: ويل لأهل المعاصي من أهل القبور

rows.speaker: أبو صالح وغيره
rows.claim: They explain min warāʾihim as meaning ahead of them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح وغيره في قوله تعالى: {ومن ورائهم} يعني: أمامهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid defines the barzakh as the barrier between this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: البرزخ: الحاجز ما بين الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: The dead are between the two worlds: neither sharing worldly eating and drinking nor receiving the next life's recompense.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: البرزخ: ما بين الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو صخر
rows.claim: Abū Ṣakhr identifies the barzakh with the graves, where people remain between worldly life and the afterlife until resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صخر: البرزخ: المقابر، لا هم في الدنيا، ولا هم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barzakh is a threat of its punishment to these dying wrongdoers, like the threats of Hell and a severe punishment behind people in 45:10 and 14:17.
rows.anchor: تهديد لهؤلاء المحتضرين من الظلمة بعذاب البرزخ، كما قال: {من ورائهم جهنم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barzakh punishment continues until resurrection; a hadith says the dead person continues to be punished in the earth.
rows.anchor: أي: يستمر به العذاب إلى يوم البعث، كما جاء في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the resurrection blast, kinship will not help: a parent will not pity or defend a child, even when the relative was once dearest.
rows.anchor: لا تنفع الأنساب يومئذ، ولا يرثي والد لولده، ولا يلوي عليه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: God will call those with claims against others to collect them; people will welcome a claim even against a parent, child, or spouse, however small.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: إذا كان يوم القيامة جمع الله الأولين والآخرين ثم نادى مناد

rows.speaker: المسور بن مخرمة
rows.claim: The Prophet says Fāṭima is part of him and that his kinship ties will endure at the Resurrection while other lineages end; Ibn Kathīr notes a related sound report in both Ṣaḥīḥs.
rows.anchor: عن المسور -هو ابن مخرمة-رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: فاطمة بضعة مني

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet says his kinship remains joined in this life and the next and he will precede people at the watering place; he knows their ancestry, but says they changed religion after him.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول على هذا المنبر

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar says he married Umm Kulthūm, daughter of ʿAlī, because he heard that every bond and lineage ends at the Resurrection except the Prophet's.
rows.anchor: لما تزوج أم كلثوم بنت علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar says every lineage and marriage bond ends on the Last Day except the Prophet's lineage and affinity.
rows.anchor: عن محمد ابن عباد بن جعفر، سمعت ابن عمر يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says the Prophet asked that anyone he married into or who married into his community be with him in Paradise, and God granted it.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن عبد الله بن عمرو مرفوعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A person whose good deeds outweigh bad deeds by even one is among those with heavy scales.
rows.anchor: من رجحت حسناته على سيئاته ولو بواحدة، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful are those saved from Hell and admitted to Paradise.
rows.anchor: الذين فازوا فنجوا من النار وأدخلوا الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the successful as obtaining what they sought and escaping what they feared.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أولئك الذين فازوا بما طلبوا، ونجوا من شر ما منه هربوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light scales mean bad deeds outweigh good deeds, leaving their owners failed, ruined, and bankrupt.
rows.anchor: أي: ثقلت سيئاته على حسناته

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A report says an angel calls out the eternal felicity or misery of each person according to the balance's weight; Ibn Kathīr grades its chain weak because Dāwūd al-Muḥabbar is abandoned.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت البناني وجعفر بن زيد ومنصور بن زاذان، عن أنس بن مالك يرفعه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned are called lasting residents of Hell who do not depart.
rows.anchor: أي: ماكثون، دائمون مقيمون لا يظعنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question exposes how little of their short worldly lives they spent worshipping God; patience in that brief life would have brought the pious believers' success.
rows.anchor: منبها لهم على ما أضاعوه في عمرهم القصير في الدنيا من طاعة الله تعالى وعبادته وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they stayed a day or part of a day and are told to ask those who count the time.
rows.anchor: أي: كم كانت إقامتكم في الدنيا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever the estimate, their life was brief; had they known, they would not have preferred the fleeting world or earned God's anger, and patient worship would have won them the believers' success.
rows.anchor: أي: مدة يسيرة على كل تقدير

rows.speaker: أيفع بن عبد الكلاعي
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that, after the two groups enter their abodes, the people of Paradise call one brief day a good bargain for mercy and bliss, while the people of Hell made a bad bargain for fire and wrath.
rows.anchor: عن أيفع بن عبد الكلاعي؛ أنه سمعه يخطب الناس فقال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن الله إذا أدخل أهل الجنة الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first gently drives newly formed clouds, gathers their scattered parts, piles them atop one another, and sends rain through them.
rows.anchor: يسوق السحاب أول ما ينشئها وهي ضعيفة، وهو الإزجاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read the phrase as rain emerging through the cloud's openings.
rows.anchor: وكذا (1) قرأها ابن عباس والضحاك

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr describes winds that sweep the earth, raise clouds, assemble them, and fertilize them with rain-bearing water; Ibn Abī Ḥātim and al-Ṭabarī transmit this account.
rows.anchor: قال عبيد بن عمير الليثي: يبعث الله المثيرة فتقم الأرض قما، ثم يبعث الله الناشئة فتنشئ السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians parse the three min particles as origin, partitive, and explanatory if hail comes from mountain-like formations in the sky; on the cloud interpretation, the second min is also origin and apposition to the first.
rows.anchor: قال بعض النحاة: "من" الأولى: لابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hail and rain may strike as mercy and be withheld as delayed rain; alternatively, hail may punish by scattering fruit and destroying crops and trees, while its being withheld is mercy.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد بقوله: {فيصيب به}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightning's intense light nearly snatches sight when someone follows or looks directly at it.
rows.anchor: يكاد ضوء برقه من شدته يخطف الأبصار إذا اتبعته وتراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God controls the night and day, alternately lengthening one and shortening the other in cycles by His command, power, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فيأخذ من طول هذا في قصر هذا حتى يعتدلا ثم يأخذ من هذا في هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of night and day is evidence of God's greatness for people of insight, as also stated in 3:190 and the following verses.
rows.anchor: أي: لدليلا على عظمته تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Abū Ṣāliḥ, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda identify the celestial burūj as great stars.
rows.anchor: وهي الكواكب العظام -في قول مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وأبي صالح، والحسن، وقتادة

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس ومحمد بن كعب وإبراهيم النخعي والأعمش
rows.claim: Another view, transmitted from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, al-Nakhaʿī, and al-Aʿmash, identifies the burūj as celestial castles for guarding the sky; it is also reported from Abū Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي قصور في السماء للحرس، يروى هذا عن علي، وابن عباس، ومحمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great-stars interpretation is clearer, though both views can be reconciled if those stars are the castles for the guards; he links this to 67:5.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أظهر. اللهم إلا أن يكون الكواكب العظام هي قصور للحرس، فيجتمع القولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun is the luminous lamp in the sky, as in 78:13.
rows.anchor: وهي الشمس المنيرة، التي هي كالسراج في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon shines with a distinct kind of light from the sun, as the verses 10:5 and 71:15–16 also say.
rows.anchor: أي: مضيئا مشرقا بنور آخر ونوع وفن آخر، غير نور الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day succeed one another continuously: when one goes, the other arrives, as also described in 14:33, 7:54, and 36:40.
rows.anchor: أي: يخلف كل واحد منهما الآخر، يتعاقبان لا يفتران. إذا ذهب هذا جاء هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their alternation times worship: a person who misses a devotional portion at night can make it up by day, or vice versa; a sound hadith also describes God's nightly and daytime acceptance of repentance.
rows.anchor: جعلهما يتعاقبان، توقيتا لعبادة عباده له، فمن فاته عمل في الليل استدركه في النهار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: ʿUmar lengthened his Duḥā prayer to complete or make up his regular portion, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: أن عمر بن الخطاب أطال صلاة الضحى، فقيل له: صنعت اليوم شيئا لم تكن تصنعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says missed worship at night may be performed in the day, and missed daytime worship at night; ʿIkrima, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and al-Ḥasan agree.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda explain khilfatan as differing in character: one is dark and the other bright.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وقتادة: {خلفة} أي: مختلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends winds that raise clouds, perhaps from the sea or wherever He wills, then spreads and enlarges them from a small cloud to fill the horizon; sometimes they arrive heavy with water, as in 7:57.
rows.anchor: إما من البحر على ما ذكره غير واحد، أو مما يشاء الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو عمرو بن العلاء ومطر الوراق وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, Maṭar al-Warrāq, and Qatāda say kisafan means pieces or fragments.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وأبو عمرو بن العلاء، ومطر الوراق، وقتادة: يعني قطعا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says kisafan means accumulated or piled up.
rows.anchor: قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another interpretation describes the clouds as black with water, dense and heavy, and close to the ground.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: أسود من كثرة الماء، تراه مدلهما ثقيلا قريبا من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain emerges from within the clouds, and those who need it rejoice when it reaches them.
rows.anchor: أي: فترى المطر -وهو القطر -يخرج من بين ذلك السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipients had long been despairing of rain; its arrival during need therefore made a great impression.
rows.anchor: أن هؤلاء القوم الذين أصابهم هذا المطر كانوا قنطين أزلين من نزول المطر إليهم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr, reporting one grammatical view, calls min qablihi an emphatic repetition.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن جرير: هو تأكيد. وحكاه عن بعض أهل العربية

rows.speaker: آخرون من النحاة
rows.claim: Other grammarians take the first phrase to mean before the rain fell and min qablihi to mean before its descent.
rows.anchor: قبل أن ينزل عليهم المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers a reading where the people needed rain before it fell and had repeatedly watched its season pass, until it came suddenly after despair.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك من دلالة التأسيس، ويكون معنى الكلام: أنهم كانوا محتاجين إليه قبل نزوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is God's mercy that revives dead earth, and this is evidence that He can revive the dead; He has power over everything.
rows.anchor: ثم نبه بذلك على إحياء الأجساد بعد موتها وتفرقها وتمزقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a dry wind yellows a grown crop, people respond with ingratitude and deny earlier blessings, as in 56:63–67.
rows.anchor: يابسة على الزرع الذي زرعوه، ونبت وشب واستوى على سوقه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmr says there are eight winds: four merciful winds—dispersing, bringing good news, sending, and spreading—and four punitive winds, two on land and two at sea.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: الرياح ثمانية، أربعة منها رحمة، وأربعة عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God's choice, winds can bring gentleness and mercy, announce mercy, and fertilize clouds with water as a male fertilizes a female; or they can be sterile, destructive punishment, with varied directions and effects.
rows.anchor: فإذا شاء سبحانه وتعالى حركه بحركة الرحمة فجعله رخاء ورحمة وبشرى بين يدي رحمته

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says the wind is controlled from the second earth; a request to destroy ʿĀd with a bull-nostril-sized wind is limited to a ring's measure, linked to 51:42. Ibn Kathīr calls it rare and its Prophetic attribution objectionable, preferring it as Ibn ʿAmr's words.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings pass through stages from dust, sperm, embryo, and fetus to a weak newborn, then childhood, youth, strength, and finally aging, weakness, and gray hair; God acts as He wills.
rows.anchor: أصله من تراب، ثم من نطفة، ثم من علقة، ثم من مضغة، ثم يصير عظاما

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar confirms to ʿAṭiyya that he recited the verse to the Prophet as ʿAṭiyya recited it to him, preserving that recitation; Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī transmit it, with al-Tirmidhī grading it ḥasan.
rows.anchor: قال: قرأت على ابن عمر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers display ignorance in both lives: they worship idols here and later swear they stayed only an hour, hoping to escape the proof against them.
rows.anchor: ومقصودهم هم بذلك عدم قيام الحجة عليهم، وأنهم لم ينظروا حتى يعذر إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of knowledge and faith answer that the disbelievers remained recorded in God's book of deeds from creation until resurrection, but did not know it.
rows.anchor: في كتاب الله} أي: في كتاب الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day the wrongdoers' excuses will not help and they will not be returned to worldly life, as 41:24 says.
rows.anchor: أي: ولا هم يرجعون إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers will not be put to death or have Hell's punishment reduced; the Qur'an and a sound Muslim report say its permanent inhabitants neither die nor live, while they plead for death and remain in torment.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {لا يموت فيها ولا يحيا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the recompense for everyone who disbelieves in their Lord and denies the truth.
rows.anchor: أي: هذا جزاء كل من كفر بربه وكذب بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's people cry out for return to do good, but God knows they would repeat their former sins; He refuses their plea, as also stated in 40:11–12.
rows.anchor: وقد علم الرب، جل جلاله، أنه لو ردهم إلى الدار الدنيا، لعادوا لما نهوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their allotted lives were long enough for anyone willing to benefit from truth to remember it.
rows.anchor: أي: أوما عشتم في الدنيا أعمارا لو كنتم ممن ينتفع بالحق لانتفعتم به

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr selects the report from Ibn ʿAbbās that the age at which a person is given enough time to reflect is forty years.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو اختيار ابن جرير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second route from Ibn ʿAbbās gives sixty years; Ibn Kathīr says this report is sounder and correct, supported by hadith.
rows.anchor: فهذه الرواية أصح عن ابن عباس، وهي الصحيحة في نفس الأمر أيضا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī also identifies sixty years as the age meant by the verse.
rows.anchor: عن علي، رضي الله عنه، أنه قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Ibn ʿAbbās says those reaching sixty will be called on Judgment Day, referring to the age in this verse.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr questions the report about the call to sixty-year-olds because of Ibrāhīm ibn al-Faḍl's condition.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث فيه نظر؛ لحال إبراهيم بن الفضل

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says God has excused a person who reaches sixty or seventy years.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من بني غفار، عن سعيد المقبري، عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A route through Abū Ḥāzim and Abū Hurayra reports that a person reaching sixty has received God's full excuse in life.
rows.anchor: حدثنا أبو حازم، عن سعيد المقبري، عن أبي هريرة قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Bazzār transmits from Abū Hurayra the report that sixty years is the age at which God has excused a person.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، عن سعيد المقبري، عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A route through Ibn ʿAjlān from Abū Hurayra says that anyone reaching sixty has been given an excuse in life.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد المقبري، عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr accepts the hadith through these routes, preferring al-Bukhārī's authentication over al-Ṭabarī's reservation.
rows.anchor: فقد صح هذا الحديث من هذه الطرق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says life's struggle falls between sixty and seventy and few of the community reach seventy; Ibn Kathīr calls its chain weak.
rows.anchor: عن المقبري، عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الأطباء
rows.claim: Some physicians say natural lifespan is 120 years, with growth until sixty and decline and senility thereafter; an unnamed poet's verse illustrates the loss of youthful pleasure by sixty.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن العمر الطبيعي عند الأطباء مائة وعشرون سنة، فالإنسان لا يزال في ازدياد إلى كمال الستين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report says the community's lifespans are generally sixty to seventy, with few exceeding that; al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah transmit it, and al-Tirmidhī calls it ḥasan gharīb.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أعمار أمتي ما بين الستين

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzār says the report about the community's age span is unique through this chain and its transmitter ʿUthmān ibn Maṭar is weak.
rows.anchor: لا يروى بهذا اللفظ إلا بهذا الإسناد، وعثمان بن مطر من أهل البصرة ليس بقوي

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa asks the Prophet about the community's lifespans; the reply gives fifty to sixty and invokes God's mercy on those reaching seventy or eighty.
rows.anchor: عن ربعي عن حذيفة أنه قال: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's lifespan is most famously reported as sixty-three years, though sixty and sixty-five are also reported.
rows.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيح أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عاش ثلاثا وستين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو جعفر الباقر وقتادة وسفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, al-Bāqir, Qatāda, and Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna identify the warner as gray hair.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وأبي جعفر الباقر، وقتادة، وسفيان بن عيينة أنهم قالوا: يعني: الشيب

rows.speaker: السدي وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd identify the warner as the Messenger; Ibn Zayd cites 53:56.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي، وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: يعني به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن جرير
rows.claim: A sounder report from Qatāda says both a long lifetime and the messengers were used as proof; Ibn Jarīr prefers the Messenger interpretation, supported by 43:77–78, 17:15, and 67:8–9.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الصحيح عن قتادة، فيما رواه شيبان، عنه أنه قال: احتج عليهم بالعمر والرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to taste the punishment for disobeying the prophets during their lives; no helper can rescue them from torment, restraints, and chains.
rows.anchor: أي: فذوقوا عذاب النار جزاء على مخالفتكم للأنبياء في مدة أعماركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the unseen of heaven and earth, including hidden thoughts and inner intentions, and will repay each person for their deeds.
rows.anchor: وأنه يعلم ما تكنه السرائر وتنطوي عليه الضمائر، وسيجازي كل عامل بعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes generations succeed earlier peoples, as also stated in 27:62.
rows.anchor: أي: يخلف قوم لآخرين قبلهم، وجيل لجيل قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harm of disbelief returns to the disbeliever; continued disbelief increases God's anger and the unbelievers' loss, whereas believers who live and act well rise in rank, reward, and God's love.
rows.anchor: أي: فإنما يعود وبال ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As people live longer, they return from strength to weakness and from activity to incapacity, as in 30:54 and 22:5.
rows.anchor: كلما طال عمره رد إلى الضعف بعد القوة والعجز بعد النشاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This world is a place of passage, not permanence; reflecting on life's progression shows people were made for the lasting afterlife.
rows.anchor: الإخبار عن هذه الدار بأنها دار زوال وانتقال، لا دار دوام واستقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a fragment from an unnamed Arab poet's poem in al-Ḥamāsa; the excerpt supplies no further gloss.
rows.anchor: من رجال أعزة … علينا وهم كانوا أعق وأظلما

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: When news was delayed, the Prophet quoted a hemistich by Ṭarafa; Aḥmad and al-Nasāʾī transmit it, and al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا استراث الخبر، تمثل فيه ببيت طرفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also reports the Prophet quoting the same line from Ṭarafa's famous Muʿallaqa; another version is related from ʿĀʾisha.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل من الأشعار

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet composed only one line, a hopeful saying; al-Mizzī calls this report objectionable because its transmitters are unknown to him.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، قالت: ما جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت شعر قط

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Another report says poetry was the Prophet's most disliked speech, though he sometimes reversed a line's halves and said he was no poet; al-Bukhārī corrects the wording in the report.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: قيل لعائشة: هل كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل بشيء من الشعر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports ʿĀʾisha's account that the Prophet quoted Ṭarafa but reversed the line's wording; Abū Bakr corrected him, and he said he was no poet and poetry was not fitting for him.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: بلغني أن عائشة سئلت: هل كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتمثل بشيء من الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authentic reports show the Prophet voicing lines by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa while joining the Companions at the Trench, the words matching their work-song.
rows.anchor: ثبت في الصحيحين أنه، عليه الصلاة والسلام، تمثل يوم حفر الخندق بأبيات عبد الله بن رواحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Ḥunayn the Prophet said he was the Prophet and son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; this and other metrical utterances happened without intending poetry.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ثبت أنه قال يوم حنين وهو راكب البغلة، يقدم بها في نحور العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When he injured his finger in a cave, he uttered a metrical line; such accidental speech does not contradict that he was not taught poetry.
rows.anchor: عن جندب بن عبد الله قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غار فنكبت أصبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught the Prophet the inimitable Qur'an rather than poetry; claims that it was poetry, soothsaying, fabrication, or magic are false, and his nature rejected poetry as craft.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى إنما علمه القرآن العظيم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report unique to Abū Dāwūd says the Prophet did not care if he received an antidote, wore an amulet, or composed poetry himself.
rows.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن عمرو يقول

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha says poetry was the Prophet's most disliked speech; she also says he favored concise, comprehensive prayers.
rows.anchor: عن أبي نوفل قال: سألت عائشة: أكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتسامع عنده الشعر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a belly full of pus is better than one full of poetry; this route is unique to Abū Dāwūd and its chain meets the Ṣaḥīḥayn's standard, though they did not include it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لأن يمتلئ جوف أحدكم قيحا

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: A rare report says composing a line of poetry after the late-night prayer makes that night's prayer unacceptable; Ibn Kathīr interprets this as composing, not reciting, poetry.
rows.anchor: عن شداد بن أوس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من قرض بيت شعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some poetry is commendable, such as Muslim poets' satire of polytheists and poetry of wisdom, admonition, and good manners.
rows.anchor: على أن الشعر فيه ما هو مشروع، وهو هجاء المشركين الذي كان يتعاطاه شعراء الإسلام

rows.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: The Prophet said of Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt, whose poetry includes wisdom, that his poetry believed while his heart disbelieved.
rows.anchor: ومنهم أمية بن أبي الصلت الذي قال فيه النبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: صحابي
rows.claim: A Companion recited one hundred lines of Umayya's poetry to the Prophet, who encouraged him to continue after each line.
rows.anchor: وقد أنشد بعض الصحابة منه للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مائة بيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created and owns everything in heaven and earth, and makes night and day follow each other rapidly, as Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, and al-Suddī explain.
rows.anchor: وأنه مالك الملك المتصرف، فيه يقلب ليله ونهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon run until a term known to God, ending at the Resurrection; He is mighty yet forgiving to those who repent and return to Him.
rows.anchor: إلى مدة معلومة عند الله ثم تنقضي يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human groups differ in kind, language, and color while descending from Adam and his wife Eve, as also stated in 4:1.
rows.anchor: خلقكم مع اختلاف أجناسكم وأصنافكم وألسنتكم وألوانكم من نفس واحدة، وهو آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight livestock pairs are created for people from the animals' offspring: two each from sheep, goats, camels, and cattle, as listed in 6:143–144.
rows.anchor: من ظهور الأنعام ثمانية، أزواج وهي المذكورة في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the womb, a person develops from sperm to clot, then lump, flesh, bones, sinews, and veins, receives a spirit, and becomes a new creation, as in 23:14.
rows.anchor: أي: يكون أحدكم أولا نطفة، ثم يكون علقة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وأبو مالك والضحاك وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: The three darknesses are the womb, the placenta or protective covering, and the abdomen, according to Ibn ʿAbbās and the listed early authorities.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، وأبو مالك، والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator of the heavens, earth, people, and their ancestors is their Lord, sovereign and controller; only He deserves worship, so worshipping another is irrational diversion.
rows.anchor: هو الرب له الملك والتصرف (8) في جميع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's statement that he fears punishment if he disobeys God is a conditional argument that applies all the more to others; he is to worship God alone sincerely.
rows.anchor: وهذا شرط، ومعناه التعريض بغيره بطريق الأولى والأحرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship as they wish is a threat and declaration of disavowal; the real losers lose themselves and their families at the Resurrection, forever separated without reunion or joy.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضا تهديد وتبر (1) منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's people are covered by layers of fire above and below, as also described in 7:41 and 29:55.
rows.anchor: لهم من جهنم مهاد ومن فوقهم غواش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to be patient because God's promise to raise his message and give him and his followers the final outcome is true and unfailing.
rows.anchor: وعدناك أنا سنعلي كلمتك، ونجعل العاقبة لك ولمن اتبعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek forgiveness urges the wider community to seek forgiveness; evening and early morning name the late day/early night and the start of day/late night.
rows.anchor: هذا تهييج للأمة على الاستغفار

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Those arguing without authority try to defeat truth with false arguments, driven by pride and contempt for its messengers; their attempt to suppress truth will fail, so seek refuge from them in God.
rows.anchor: يدفعون الحق بالباطل، ويردون الحجج الصحيحة بالشبه الفاسدة بلا برهان ولا حجة من الله

rows.speaker: كعب وأبو العالية
rows.claim: They say the verse concerns Jews who claimed the Dajjāl would come from them and enable them to rule the earth; Abū al-ʿĀliya reads the command as seeking refuge from his trial. Ibn Kathīr calls this strange and strained.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب وأبو العالية: نزلت هذه الآية في اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must answer their Lord before the irreversible Day, which occurs instantly when God commands and has no preventer.
rows.anchor: إذا أمر بكونه فإنه كلمح البصر يكون، وليس له دافع ولا مانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No fortress or hiding place can conceal anyone from God's knowledge, sight, and power; there is no refuge except in Him, as 75:10–12 says.
rows.anchor: ليس لكم حصن تتحصنون فيه، ولا مكان يستركم وتتنكرون فيه، فتغيبون عن بصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If polytheists turn away, the Prophet is not their controller or guardian; his sole duty is to convey the message, as in 2:272 and 13:40.
rows.anchor: يعني: المشركين {فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People rejoice at ease and blessings but deny past favors when drought, punishment, or hardship strikes; a hadith illustrates this with a wife denying a husband's kindness after one bad day.
rows.anchor: أي: إذا أصابه رخاء ونعمة فرح بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer benefits in either state: gratitude during prosperity and patience in adversity are both good, according to a Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: إن أصابته سراء شكر فكان خيرا له، وإن أصابته ضراء صبر فكان خيرا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers of resurrection say only worldly life exists and people alternate between dying and living. This includes Arab polytheists, philosophers who deny creation and return, and cyclical materialists who deny a Creator and posit endless 36,000-year repetitions.
rows.anchor: المعتقدون أن في كل ستة وثلاثين ألف سنة يعود كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that time alone destroys them is unsupported conjecture; a sound divine report says God is the one who turns night and day, and people should not curse time.
rows.anchor: وما لهم بذلك من علم إن هم إلا يظنون

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God is harmed by the human who curses time, since God controls the affair and turns night and day; another wording prohibits cursing time.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Further reports from Abū Hurayra describe pre-Islamic people blaming night and day for death and life; a divine report says a human curses time while God controls night and day. Another report says God lent to a servant who refused and was insulted as 'time'.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق عن العلاء بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Abū ʿUbayda, and other imams explain that Arabs blamed and cursed time for hardship, though God actually causes those events; cursing time therefore indirectly curses God. Ibn Kathīr calls this the best explanation.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي وأبو عبيدة وغيرهما من الأئمة في تفسير قوله

rows.speaker: ابن حزم
rows.claim: Ibn Ḥazm and like-minded literalists wrongly count al-dahr as one of God's beautiful names based on this hadith.
rows.anchor: وقد غلط ابن حزم ومن نحا نحوه من الظاهرية في عدهم الدهر من الأسماء الحسنى
